about: The motion inventory (Prompt 279). Every source of time-based change in the sources, and what each does when the reader asks for reduced motion (the system setting, or Settings, Motion). tests/motionInventory.test.js scans css/ and js/ and fails on a keyframes or a scheduler that is not here, on a listed one that no longer exists, on a source marked `follows` that does not read the setting, and on a gap without its reason. e2e/a11ySweepII.spec.js reads it for the pages it runs with reduced motion. Treatments: `content` is the motion the page exists to show, with a pause control and its reduced-motion behaviour; `follows` honours the setting in code; `gap` starts by itself, has no pause and does not read the setting; `opt-in` does not start by itself; `timer`, `workload`, `once` and `capture` move nothing on screen.

css.about: All sixteen are covered by the blanket rules: under prefers-reduced-motion and under the reader's data-motion override every animation runs once in 0.01 ms and every transition is 0.01 ms (css/components.css, css/styles.css, and the unlayered :root[data-motion] rule). Two stop outright.

override.about: Where the reader's own Settings, Motion choice (Follow my device, Reduced, Step by step; `gravitas_motion`) takes effect. It is read by js/quality.js, which only the application page loads, so it reaches the application (the sandbox and the lessons in it) and nowhere else. Every other page follows the system setting alone, which the blanket rules honour on all of them. e2e/a11ySweepII.spec.js holds the list exact: a page that learns the choice fails there until its row is corrected.
override.proposal: Apply it where the theme is applied: in the script the shell stamps into every page's head (tools/shell.mjs, HEAD), three lines that set data-motion from the stored value before the first paint. It costs no JavaScript budget, and it re-stamps the 178 pages that carry the shell and their CSP hashes, which is why this sweep records it rather than doing it among the fixes.
